observation: 86 resident export entries of the qualified export reference hardware registers directly. Hooking all of them in six route windows (field with a music load, field walking, combat, post-battle, field return and the closing menu entry) shows 34 entries hit: a serial/pad transaction once per frame, root-counter reads eight times per frame, interrupt acknowledge and dispatch several times per frame, ordering-table clear and GPU DMA every frame, a VSync wait (overlay 800758d0) polling a resident entry about 1,100-3,000 times per field frame, no-wait CD command writes with interrupt-driven acknowledgement during loads, and SPU register writes while music loads. All 72 final RAM and audio artifacts of the 36 census captures equal the uninstrumented route.
interpretation: The route's hardware-facing intent falls into five native services: display submission, controller state, asynchronous disc reads with completion status, audio voice updates, and interrupt/time callbacks. The reconstruction keeps game logic above these boundaries; the disc command acknowledgement and interrupt handlers are the explicit remaining boundaries on the compared paths.
author: Claude Opus 5.5, integration owner
reviewers: Independent evidence review recomputing every count and call site from the 36 traces, checking hook derivation, guards, classification, the disc and DMA callback claims against snapshots, and non-perturbation (review-hw-census.md). Its corrections are applied: counts are entry-address hits (some entries are fragments or loop heads), the command writer is no-wait on the route with interrupt-driven acknowledgement, the VSync wait rate and location are corrected, budget-limited cells are marked, and no library names are claimed.

preconditions: Pinned Nix environment and original Disc 1 profile; frozen route input tests/reference-inputs/field23-encounter-observation.json; observation core parity 1.7.1.
Hook lists derived from the qualified resident export data references; no library identity is claimed.
commands: nix --extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes' develop path:./nix#observation-trace -c python3 tools/reference/scenario.py tests/reference-inputs/field23-encounter-observation.json --content 'discs/Xenogears disc 1.chd' --output .local/scenarios/phase1-field23-hw-WINDOW-GROUP-20260923-v5 --trace-instructions .local/execution/field-update/hw-WINDOW-GROUP.json
validation.expected: Every directly hardware-referencing resident function either appears with counts and call sites or is absent from all windows; captures do not perturb the route.
validation.actual: 34 of 86 export entries hit; per-group entry-hit counts in analysis/formats/service-boundaries.md; 72 of 72 final artifacts identical to the uninstrumented route; hook group 2 reached its callback budget in the two field windows (lower bounds, marked).
validation.tolerance: None; counts are exact within each window except the two budget-limited group-2 windows.

limitations: Sampled windows, not the whole route; counts are hits on export entry addresses, some of which are fragments or loop heads of larger routines; code reaching hardware only through unresolved pointers is not listed.
Cadence is observed on an HLE-BIOS interpreter and is not a hardware timing proof.
Display, controller, disc and audio services are not implemented natively; this records intent and boundaries only.
